title: Closed-loop control for two-qubit gates with trapped ions
abstract: State-of-the-art two-qubit gates with trapped ions employ open-loop control that rely on simplified models to precompute control sequences. Our aim is to introduce closed-loop control for two-qubit gates to correct disturbances as they occur during the gate implementation. We introduce a spectator ion into the ion chain used for quantum logic processing, where it couples with the other ions through collective motional modes. The spectator ion's position is continuously monitored by driving dipole transitions and detecting the resultant fluorescence. We show that incorporating a spectator ion is feasible for linear Paul trap implementations and is expected to reduce the two-qubit gate Bell-state preparation infidelity by an order of magnitude with the deleterious effects of position monitoring being negligible compared to the thermal effects that exist in the system, even in the absence of the spectator ions. Mathematically, we describe driven ion-trap dynamics, including the spectator ion, by a stochastic quantum master equation involving the amplitude-modulation multimode-motional coupling gate, motional drift, thermal effects, recoil from photon scattering, spontaneous decay, and light shift. Our on-the-fly control method employs reinforcement learning with the reward function based on the actual geometric phase of the spectator ion. A key advantage of our approach is that we introduce a control method that involves `learning' and correcting disturbances happening in the trap on-the-fly, thus achieving high-fidelity gates. Our approach will lead to a significantly higher two-qubit gate fidelity at a reduced calibration overhead owing to the small parameter drift in the control system.

title: Spectral characterizations of entanglement witnesses
abstract: We present a systematic investigation of the spectral properties of entanglement witnesses (EWs). Specifically, we analyze the infimum and supremum of the largest eigenvalue, the smallest eigenvalue, the negativity (defined as the absolute value of the sum of negative eigenvalues), and the squared Frobenius norm of a unit-trace (normalized) entanglement witness, along with the conditions under which these values are attained. Our study provides distinct characterizations for decomposable (DEWs) and nondecomposable entanglement witnesses (NDEWs). While these two classes share many spectral similarities, we reveal a fundamental divergence by proving that the infimum of the smallest eigenvalue can be attained by DEWs, yet remains strictly unattainable for all NDEWs. We apply the results to provide necessary conditions for an EW to possess a mirrored EW. Furthermore, we demonstrate the superior detection capability of NDEWs by proving that any non-positive-partial-transpose state beyond the two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems can be detected by an NDEW.

title: BCMT : Transformer à mémoire causale par blocs
abstract: Transformer architectures rely on dense self-attention to model long-range dependencies, but this mechanism exhibits quadratic complexity with respect to sequence length. We introduce BCMT (Blockwise Causal Memory Transformer ), an architecture for long-context language modeling that decouples local token interactions from global context propagation. Dense causal self-attention is applied independently within local blocks, while each block produces an adaptive summary aggregated through an exponential causal memory. This memory is subsequently injected back into the token representations, enabling efficient propagation of long-range contextual information without relying on explicit global attention. Unlike standard Transformers and recurrent memory architectures, BCMT maintains neither dense interactions between distant tokens nor learned memory states. Its memory mechanism is fully parallelizable and remains compatible with standard implementations of dense self-attention. Experiments on language modeling with context lengths of up to 1024 tokens show that BCMT achieves validation performance comparable to that of Dense Transformers while significantly improving training throughput and reducing memory consumption. An ablation study further confirms that these improvements arise from the proposed memory mechanism. These results demonstrate that an exponential causal memory constructed from block summaries provides an effective alternative to dense global attention mechanisms for long-context language modeling.

title: A Marchian Perspective on Exploratory Play as a Mode of Human–AI Interaction
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual framework to explain how play functions as a mode of exploration in human–AI interaction. Building on March’s Technology of Foolishness and the organizational play literature, we theorize exploratory play as a cognitive and behavioral orientation that relaxes goals, rules, memory, and evaluative constraints in order to enable wide-ranging and itinerant search. We first reinterpret March’s framework in relation to contemporary theories of play and creativity, then illustrate its relevance through historical and contemporary cases of tinkering. We extend this framework to human interaction with generative AI, arguing that large language models introduce a novel environment for exploratory play by enabling rapid linguistic prototyping, iterative reframing, and safe experimentation. Rather than treating AI as a substitute for human creativity, we show how human intuition, imagination, and sensemaking remain central to guiding exploration and recognizing value. The framework offers a theoretical lens for understanding how human–AI interaction may increase the conditions under which unexpected insights and novel strategic possibilities emerge.

title: Research on Unbalanced Data Classification Algorithm Based on Boundary Simulation SMOTE
abstract: Classifying imbalanced datasets poses a significant challenge in machine learning, as traditional classifiers tend to favor the majority class, leading to poor recognition rates for the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by interpolating between minority instances, its blind sampling mechanism often creates synthetic samples in overlapping areas or majority class regions, resulting in blurred decision boundaries and noise amplification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling method named Boundary Simulation SMOTE (BS-SMOTE). The core idea of BS-SMOTE is to identify and simulate the behavioral boundary of classifiers to guide the generation of synthetic instances. By analyzing the local neighborhood structure of both majority and minority classes, the algorithm filters out isolated noise and precisely extracts critical "boundary minority samples." During the sample generation phase, a boundary constraint mechanism based on the nearest majority neighbors is introduced. This mechanism adjusts the interpolation direction to simulate the decision boundary, ensuring that synthetic samples reinforce the boundary area without invading the majority class space. Performance is evaluated using comprehensive metrics tailored for imbalanced data, including F1-Score, G-Mean, and AUC. This approach effectively refines the decision boundary, prevents class overlapping, and significantly enhances the classifier's generalization capabilities on imbalanced data.

title: An Instance Rewriting SMOTE Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Classification
abstract: Class imbalance poses a significant challenge in machine learning, as standard classifiers tend to favor the majority class and exhibit poor generalization on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue, its linear interpolation mechanism often introduces noise and exacerbates class overlapping by neglecting the underlying manifold structure of high-dimensional data. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling method named Instance Rewriting SMOTE (IR-SMOTE). Instead of generating synthetic samples via blind interpolation along lines connecting neighbors, IR-SMOTE focuses on "rewriting the structure of existing instances." The algorithm uncovers the local geometric neighborhood of minority samples, computes a local centroid, and derives structural deviation vectors to capture unique topological characteristics. By introducing a dynamic rewriting control factor based on region sparsity, IR-SMOTE deconstructs and rewrites minority instances through radial scaling and longitudinal feature recombination within a localized coordinate system. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this rewriting mechanism preserves the intrinsic data manifold and creates high-quality, diverse minority instances without penetrating majority class boundaries. IR-SMOTE provides a more robust and effective solution for expanding decision boundaries and enhancing classification performance on imbalanced datasets.

title: Dynamic Density SMOTE: A Dynamic Density Update Mechanism Based on Training Feedback for Imbalanced Data Classification
abstract: Imbalanced data classification poses a significant challenge in the field of machine learning. The traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) expands the scale of minority class samples through linear interpolation between nearest neighbors, but its sampling probability is usually based on static density estimation. In iterative training or dynamic learning tasks, the fixed density estimation fails to adapt to the shifts of classification boundaries, which easily introduces noise samples into overlapping regions. This paper proposes a dynamic density synthetic over-sampling technique, named Dynamic Density SMOTE (DD-SMOTE). The algorithm treats the local density of samples as a dynamic variable that updates alongside the training process. By integrating the current classifier feedback, boundary movements, and shifts in sample distribution, the algorithm dynamically adjusts the sampling weights of minority class samples. Through the establishment of a dynamic density update model, DD-SMOTE can accurately identify core imbalanced regions and adaptively adjust the over-sampling strategy during training. Theoretical analysis indicates that this dynamic update and closed-loop feedback mechanism make the distribution of synthetic samples fit the real-time requirements of the classifier more precisely, thereby effectively improving the generalization ability of minority class decision boundaries.

title: The Asian Language Tax: Quantifying the Cost, Context, and Recall Penalty of Tokenizing Lower-Resource Asian Languages in Frontier LLMs
abstract: Commercial large language models bill, throttle, and budget context per token. Yet tokenizers assign more subword tokens to the same meaning in some languages than in others, so speakers of high-fertility languages pay a structural penalty before a model is ever invoked. This work measures that penalty across 16 Asian languages spanning seven language families and twelve scripts (Latin, Devanagari, Bengali, Sinhala, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Thai), using parallel corpora so that the language effect is isolated from content. Contributions: - Same-content cost ratio across 16 Asian languages and 10 production tokenizers on FLORES-200 dev (n=997), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Median 8.9x on cl100k_base for the 11 non-Latin scripts, up to 11.7x for Burmese. - Bytes-per-token (BPT) metric introduced for cross-script-fair comparison. - A 4,000-cell needle-in-haystack recall benchmark with script-native markers, across 5 frontier OpenRouter models x 16 languages x 5 fill levels up to 131k tokens. - Headline finding: recall on non-Latin scripts collapses to 0-2/10 already at 4k tokens for 4 of 5 tested models — well inside every model's context window. gemini-2.5 lash breaks the pattern with 84.5% pooled recall on the same grid, indicating a vendor-level training/serving choice rather than an intrinsic limit. - Wall-clock latency penalty benchmark (800 measured trials + 240 warmup calls). Pooled Pearson r between cost_ratio and latency_ratio = 0.314 — notably weaker than prior African-language findings — with per-model range -0.19 (qwen) to +0.74 (llama-3.1-8b). Release artefacts: - Python package: https://github.com/Helmo21/asia-fertility (MIT) - HuggingFace dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Helmo21/asia-fertility (CC-BY-SA 4.0) - Manifest with SHA256 of config, pinned price + FX snapshots, tokenizer versions per run. This record bundles the preprint (PDF + LaTeX source), the three benchmark CSVs (leaderboard, NIAH v0.3, latency), and the study manifest so any figure in the paper can be reconstructed byte-for-byte.

title: First Look at Quantum Circuits: Implications for Defence, Cybersecurity, and Military Education
abstract: In this paper we present a structured framework for introducing quantum programming into defence-oriented education and we argue that early literacy in quantum technologies is essential for future military officers. Motivated by the rapid progress of quantum processors and the growing impact of quantum algorithms on cryptanalysis, optimisation, and data processing, we outline both the opportunities and security risks that quantum computing brings to national defence systems. The first part of paper provides a concise introduction to quantum computing fundamentals, including the nature of qubits, superposition and measurement, the action of key quantum gates, and the construction of multi-qubit states through tensor products. The second part demonstrates these principles through simple quantum circuits implemented in Python using Qiskit, illustrating phenomena such as the creation of a maximally entangled two-qubit state and an analogue of the Monty Hall paradox. By combining mathematical concepts with hands-on experimentation in a controlled simulation environment, the proposed teaching approach highlights the operational relevance of quantum thinking for cadets preparing for roles in cyber defence, signals and communications, electronic warfare, and intelligence analysis. The article concludes that integrating quantum programming into military education enhances technological preparedness and strengthens the ability of defence institutions to anticipate quantum-era challenges, including the transition to quantum-resistant cryptography and the incorporation of quantum technologies into multidomain operations.

title: Eﬀicient Long-Context Retrieval Systems via Dynamic Sparse Attention
abstract: Large language models now admit inputs far longer than a single query, so a model can reason jointly over whole collections of long documents. Context windows are finite, however, and so retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) closes that gap by indexing the corpus and retrieving the relevant evidence from it. While long-context RAG applications benefit from both corpus scale and context length, the key-value (KV) cache makes serving them impractical due to its linear growth with sequence length and batch size. Serving systems like RetroInfer use dynamic sparse attention (DSA) to address that bottleneck, offloading the cache and attending at each decode step to a subset of its entries. However, the way DSA reshapes the quality-cost trade-offs of end-to-end long-context RAG remains underexplored. This thesis characterizes RetroInfer-served long-context RAG on FinanceBench and LongBench v2 across three models (8B-72B), then redesigns its KV selection on that basis. We show that quality peaked at a model-dependent context length that grew with model size, and that sparse attention held accuracy near full attention while cutting GPU KV-cache memory 2-12×. We traced its decode overhead to host-side cache management, and found that reranking improved the trade-off only at short context. Among the RetroInfer design choices and mechanism assumptions tested, segmented k-means clustering proved unnecessary: a positional partitioning paired with an upper-bound scorer matched or exceeded both k-means and full attention across the three models, at minimal serving overhead. The scoring rule, not the partitioning, is the decisive choice in KV selection. We argue that retrieval can make long-context RAG feasible when used over both the corpus and the KV cache, and that DSA does not require a sophisticated partitioning method such as k-means.

This thesis characterizes RetroInfer-served long-context RAG on FinanceBench and LongBench v2 across three models (8B-72B), then redesigns its KV selection on that basis. We show that quality peaked at a model-dependent context length that grew with model size, and that sparse attention held accuracy near full attention while cutting GPU KV-cache memory 2-12×. We traced its decode overhead to host-side cache management, and found that reranking improved the trade-off only at short context. Among the RetroInfer design choices and mechanism assumptions tested, segmented k-means clustering proved unnecessary: a positional partitioning paired with an upper-bound scorer matched or exceeded both k-means and full attention across the three models, at minimal serving overhead. The scoring rule, not the partitioning, is the decisive choice in KV selection. We argue that retrieval can make long-context RAG feasible when used over both the corpus and the KV cache, and that DSA does not require a sophisticated partitioning method such as k-means.

title: Neuro-Fuzzy Modeling of Decision-Making in Cyber Defense Exercises Using ANFIS and Synthetic Data Augmentation
abstract: Decision-making in cyber defense exercises (CDX) is shaped by technical, emotional, motivational, and collaborative human factors under uncertainty and time pressure. This study proposes a human-centered Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) framework to model and predict Counterfactual Decision Reflection (CDR) outcomes in CDX environments. Two complementary datasets representing technical, emotional, motivational, and teamwork-related dimensions were collected from the international Lithuanian Armed Forces cyber defense exercise Amber Mist 2024 and analyzed using Spearman correlation, 3D regression surface modeling, fuzzy rule extraction, and ANFIS prediction to investigate the relationship between human factors and CDR. The results demonstrated that teamwork, communication, and collaboration have a stronger influence on decision stability than isolated technical competencies. Baseline ANFIS evaluation indicated that triangular membership functions provided the best generalization, while generalized bell functions achieved the lowest training errors. To improve model robustness, multiple synthetic data augmentation methods were evaluated. The augmented ANFIS models substantially improved predictive performance, reducing testing error values significantly. The findings confirm that synthetic-data-enhanced neuro-fuzzy modeling provides an effective and interpretable framework for analyzing human-centered cybersecurity decision-making processes in cyber defense exercises.

title: A bilingual sentiment analysis platform for medication reviews
abstract: In contemporary healthcare systems, patient feedback constitutes a valuable source of information for understanding real- world medication use and treatment effectiveness. Sentiment analysis contributes to pharmacovigilance by facilitating the detection of adverse effects and strengthening drug safety monitoring through the systematic interpretation of patient-reported experiences. However, several persistent challenges restrict its full potential. The lack of comprehensive platforms for analyzing patient-reported outcomes limits healthcare providers’ ability to derive meaningful insights into medication effectiveness. Furthermore, most existing research remains predominantly in English, while other important languages—particularly Arabic—receive comparatively limited attention. This imbalance is exacerbated by the scarcity of Arabic-language resources and annotated datasets, which continues to hinder the development of inclusive, linguistically diverse healthcare solutions. To address these gaps, we introduce BI-PharmaP, a bilingual platform for analyzing medication reviews in both English and Arabic. The platform is structured around four key components: (i) a unified interface that enables patients and healthcare providers to query and analyze existing feedback, explore comments and statistical visualizations, and submit new reviews; (ii) a bilingual processing strategy that ensures consistent handling of English and Arabic inputs, including dialectal variations; (iii) a fine-tuned RoBERTa model for sentiment classification; and (iv) an active learning loop that incorporates user-validated corrections to iteratively refine the model’s performance. In addition, the platform facilitates the continuous expansion of a bilingual labeled review corpus, thereby supporting future research and model development. Collectively, BI-PharmaP provides a scalable and adaptive framework that enhances pharmacovigilance, strengthens drug safety monitoring, and advances patient-centered pharmaceutical research.

title: SECURE AND PRIVACY PRESERVING FEDERATED LEARNING USING GENERATIVE ADVERSARIAL NETWORKS FOR HEALTH CARE SYSTEM
authors: S aacute nchez-de la Rosa R
abstract: With the accelerated digitization of healthcare systems, there has been the creation of extensive medical data of sensitive information within distributed institutions. Although machine learning methods have the potential to greatly enhance the level of diagnosing diseases and clinical decision-making, the conventional centralized learning methods involve the aggregation of patient data into a central server, which is highly questionable in terms of privacy and security. Federated Learning (FL) is a system that makes decentralized model training possible, allowing local models to be trained within healthcare facilities, but with no raw data exchange; all the same, FL is susceptible to privacy attacks, including model inversion and gradient leakage. The paper will suggest a safe and privacy-sensitive federated learning system with the improvement of Generative Adversarial Network (GANs) to healthcare applications. GANs are used on the client-side to produce privacy-sensitive synthetic data that supports the statistical characteristics of actual medical data. These protected representations are used to train local models and only encrypted model updates are transmitted to a central server by secure aggregation mechanisms. The experimental outcomes of datasets related to healthcare data show that the proposed solution is effective in minimizing the risks of privacy and preserving the competitive predictive accuracy, which makes it applicable to the real-life application of collaborative healthcare analytics.

title: Learnable Multi-Attribute Gradual Semantics for Predicting Persuasion in Argumentative Debates
abstract: Gradual semantics for weighted bipolar argumentation provide a principled framework for modelling argumentative reasoning, yet existing approaches remain mostly scalar, fixed, and weakly grounded in empirical data. We introduce learnable multi-attribute gradual semantics for persuasion prediction in argumentative debates. Our approach builds a dataset of 600 textual debates converted into multi-attribute argumentation graphs enriched with multi-dimensional features on nodes and relations. Building on this representation, we propose learnable aggregation operators that distinguish intrinsic quality from persuasive strategy dimensions. Experiments show that the learned semantics achieve competitive performance with neural and LLM-based baselines while preserving interpretability.

title: Supervised Clustered Interpretability: Explainable Subgroup Discovery via Cluster Separation and Partial Dependence Disparity
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the novel concept of clustered interpretability to enhance the transparency and explainability of artificial intelligence models in data sets with heterogeneous feature-outcome relationships. Traditional interpretability techniques often focus on global or local explanations, providing either an overview of the model’s behavior across the data set or explanations for individual predictions. However, these approaches can fall short when modeling clustered data sets, in which interpretable feature-outcome relationships across subgroups are desirable. Furthermore, existing research on interpretable clustering generally focuses on the interpretability of cluster assignment decisions in unsupervised settings rather than the interpretability of feature effects in supervised settings. To address this gap, our framework proposes a novel metric—the separation-disparity index—that prioritizes between-cluster variance while minimizing unnecessary heterogeneity in the clusters’ feature-outcome relationships. We use this metric alongside particle swarm optimization (PSO) to learn interpretable cluster solutions, incorporating novel modifications into the PSO algorithm to encourage high-quality solutions. We then demonstrate the value of our framework on synthetic data and a real-world healthcare data set of Parkinson’s disease patients. History: This paper has been accepted by Kaushik Dutta for the Special Issue on Responsible AI and Data Science for Social Good. Supplemental Material: The software that supports the findings of this study is available within the paper and its Supplemental Information ( https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/ijoc.2024.0657 ) as well as from the IJOC GitHub software repository ( https://github.com/INFORMSJoC/2024.0657 ). The complete IJOC Software and Data Repository is available at https://informsjoc.github.io/ .

title: Neuro-LENS: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework Integrating Incomplete Background Knowledge and Deep Learning
abstract: In this study, we propose Neuro-LENS, a neuro-symbolic evidence-based logic and symbolic reasoning framework that combines incomplete symbolic knowledge with neural learning to address ambiguity and improve the accuracy and interpretability of the results. We explore three strategies for integrating symbolic reasoning with deep learning and evaluate their effectiveness in practical settings: (i) applying the symbolic component to the neural output (neural-to-symbolic chaining); (ii) generating additional neural input features through symbolic rules (symbolic-to-neural chaining); (iii) creating an ensemble reasoning model (parallel neural-symbolic integration). The potential of the proposed Neuro-LENS framework is demonstrated on two real-world use cases: scene classification with abandoned object detection and prognostic health monitoring in vehicle failure prediction.

title: Evaluating oversampling methods for imbalanced Arabic dialect identification
abstract: This study investigates whether oversampling is a reliable solution for severe class imbalance in Arabic dialect identification. Using the Shami Corpus as a controlled testbed, we demonstrate that conventional oversampling often fails in high-dimensional sparse text spaces, but density based cluster filtering can effectively resolve this. We conduct a comparative evaluation of SMOTE, clustering-guided variants (ASTRA-SMOTE and SMOTE-RADIANT), and a cost-sensitive ClassWeight approach under an identical 5,644-dimensional feature-engineering pipeline using LightGBM and XGBoost. On the held-out test set, standard SMOTE and class weighting frequently distorted decision boundaries, yielding inconsistent gains across models. In contrast, SMOTE-RADIANT yields a statistically significant macro-F1 improvement for LightGBM (0.8539 vs. 0.8526 on the original data) with a large effect size (r = 0.511), successfully rescuing minority dialects without degrading the majority class. These findings suggest that while oversampling is not universally reliable in sparse text spaces, coupling it with density-based noise neutralization (RADIANT) provides a robust and interpretable alternative to deep learning models. This study provides methodological clarity and reproducible guidance for fair and inclusive Arabic NLP systems.

title: Candidate TLS Defects at the Al-Si Interface in a Superconducting Qubit from STEM-based Structure Refinement
abstract: Two-level systems (TLSs) are the dominant source of decoherence in superconducting qubits, a leading platform for quantum computing. While TLSs are believed to arise from atomic-scale tunneling defects, their precise structural origins, particularly at complex and disordered interfaces in real devices, have remained elusive. Conventional structural characterization is extremely challenging because these interfaces are non-periodic, containing steps and roughness, and device-relevant TLS defects involve only atomic motions with small energy differences. We have determined the atomic character of candidate TLSs at the Al-Si interface of a superconducting qubit using aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with experiment-constrained 3D structure modeling and computational defect searching. High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) STEM images were obtained from a disordered interface containing a prominent step defect and localized strain. Structure modeling started with 3D models created in the Ingrained framework to match the experimental projections, accounting for mistilt and uniform strain. These models were then refined using FANTASTX (Fully Automated Nanoscale To Atomistic Structure from Theory and eXperiments), a multi-objective optimizer that simultaneously minimizes disagreement with the experimental image via structural similarity and the ab initio (DFT) total system energy. Transition-state searches with the activation relaxation technique nouveau (ARTn) on the refined models identified many atomic configurations occupying double-well potentials corresponding to TLS. Statistical analysis of over 1500 TLSs shows that candidate TLS with tunneling energies and asymmetries in the range relevant to superconducting qubits (∼5 GHz) predominantly involve Al atoms located near the interface. These atoms exhibit smaller median tunneling displacements (∼0.44 Å) than the non-candidate TLS and reside in locally disordered environments with marginally longer and less dense first-neighbor shells than those of non-candidate TLSs. The most probable candidate TLSs feature cooperative motion of one or two Al atoms, and sometimes with Si, in directions largely parallel to the interface. This work provides the first direct atomic-scale insight into the structural defects that may be responsible for decoherence at a realistic, device-relevant interface. It also demonstrates a scalable, generalizable workflow for solving the atomic structure of complex, disordered interfaces by integrating aberration-corrected STEM with advanced computational refinement and defect searching. The methodology is directly applicable to other materials systems and heterointerfaces critical to quantum devices [5].

title: MAECR: a multi-head attention enhanced convolutional network for radar usage knowledge graph reasoning
abstract: Radar usage reasoning is a crucial component for enhancing situational awareness in electronic warfare. However, the increasing adaptability and intelligence of modern radar systems have resulted in a vast number of received signal parameters and complex parameter combinations, posing significant challenges for traditional models to capture the intricate relationships between radar signal parameters and their corresponding usages. To address this problem, a multi-head attention enhanced convolutional network for radar usage knowledge graph (KG) reasoning is proposed in this paper. First, structured information from the KG is utilized to more accurately represent the semantic associations between radar signals and their usages. Second, based on the ConvE architecture, a multi-head attention mechanism is incorporated to capture global dependencies among multi-dimensional radar parameters, while the convolutional module enhances sensitivity to subtle parameter variations. To evaluate the proposed model, two datasets consisting of short- and long-sequence radar signals are constructed. A series of comparative experiments are conducted to assess the model's performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline models on both datasets across mean reciprocal rank (MRR), Hits@1, and Hits@3, validating its effectiveness in modeling the “many-to-one” relationships in radar usage KG.

title: A multimodal computational pathology framework for differential diagnosis of fibro-osseous jaw lesions
abstract: ABSTRACT Fibro-osseous lesions (FOLs) of the jaws show substantial histopathological overlap, complicating diagnosis. This study developed and validated a multimodal artificial intelligence framework integrating stromal nuclear morphometry, clinicopathological variables and deep histopathological features for classifying fibrous dysplasia (FD), cemento-ossifying fibroma (COF) and cemento-osseous dysplasia (COD), and evaluated its performance alongside experienced pathologists. A multicentre retrospective cohort of 157 patients (55 FD, 55 COF and 47 COD) was analysed. Whole-slide images underwent colour normalisation and tissue and nuclear segmentation. Nuclear features were extracted using QuPath, while XGBoost with SHAP was used to evaluate structured variables and provide case-level interpretability. Image embeddings from ResNet-50, DeepLabV3 and InceptionV3 were integrated with clinicopathological and morphometric data. Model performance was assessed using five-fold patient-level cross-validation, internal validation, institution-stratified analysis and independent hold-out validation. Performance was compared with two blinded oral and maxillofacial pathologists. Nuclear area, circularity, eccentricity and mean haematoxylin optical density differed significantly between lesions (all P <0.001). ResNet-50 achieved the highest multimodal performance in internal validation, with 88.5% accuracy, κ = 0.827 and a macro-AUROC of 0.901, together with the lowest Brier score (0.094) and expected calibration error (0.036). In the independent hold-out evaluation, ResNet-50 achieved 84.6% accuracy and a macro-AUROC of 0.875. Pathologist accuracies were 47.77% and 68.15%, with limited interobserver agreement (κ=0.061). Multimodal integration enabled consistent classification of FOLs across evaluation settings. These findings highlight the importance of stromal nuclear features and support explainable multimodal artificial intelligence as a decision-support approach for morphologically overlapping jaw lesions.

title: A unified benchmark of deep learning and classical machine learning models for weather-based solar power forecasting: Balancing complexity and skill
abstract: Numerical weather prediction (NWP) is the primary input for forecasting photovoltaic (PV) power generation for lead times ranging from a few hours to several days. Data-driven and hybrid irradiance-to-power methods are considered state-of-the-art; however, it remains unclear whether the latest improvements in machine learning (ML) hold significant potential for this domain. A comparison of 12 classical ML and deep learning (DL) models is presented to compare sequence-to-sequence architectures with feature-engineered tabular regression models from various aspects. All models are implemented and optimized for seven locations, using four years of measured PV power and ECMWF weather forecasts. Results reveal that after careful implementation and proper optimization, each considered ML model is capable of achieving a skill score of 46.7-47.7% over persistence, outperforming the 40.3% skill of reference physical model chains. The most accurate forecasts are created by recurrent neural networks (RNN), including long short-term memory and gated recurrent unit setups, closely followed by Pyraformer, Informer, and Autoformer transformer variants. However, classical multilayer perceptrons (MLP) and kernel ridge regression are also great alternatives, and even easy-to-use ensemble learning algorithms, such as ExtraTrees (ET), can catch up if expert inputs with physical hybridization and temporal feature engineering are provided. The similar forecast quality suggests that model selection should rely on the joint consideration of multiple factors, including the significant computational complexity of DL models and the large sensitivity of ensemble and transformer models to their hyperparameters. Overall, physical modeling, ET, MLP, and RNN are emerging as Pareto-optimal trade-offs of accuracy and runtime.

title: Fusion: A Framework for Unified Sequential Token AdaptatIon in VisiOn TraNsformers
abstract: Vision Transformers achieve strong image classification accuracy but process all image regions with nearly the same computation, even when many regions are redundant or uninformative. Recent adaptive inference methods reduce this cost by selectively compressing tokens or terminating inference early, but combining these mechanisms often causes unstable intermediate representations and accuracy degradation. We introduce Fusion, a unified adaptive inference framework that coordinates token merging, early exiting, and token pruning through a simple staged design: tokens are merged first, confidence is evaluated next, and pruning is applied only to samples that continue inference. This ordering allows the three mechanisms to operate cooperatively rather than competitively. Fusion further includes lightweight routing modules that adapt compression strength to each input and support inference-time adjustment of the accuracy--latency trade-off without retraining. On ImageNet-1k with DeiT-S, Fusion matches or surpasses state-of-the-art adaptive ViT methods at comparable compute budgets while reducing calibration error by up to $4\times$ and inference energy by $48\%$. Experiments across ImageNet-100, CIFAR-100, and ImageNette with multiple ViT backbones demonstrate consistent transferability without dataset-specific tuning.

title: Detrimental Agnostic Entanglement: The Case Against Hardware-Efficient AnsäTze for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) for combinatorial optimization routinely employ entangling gates as a default design choice, yet the role of entanglement, in its amount and structure, remains poorly understood. This gap is particularly consequential for problems governed by diagonal Hamiltonians, whose ground states are classical product states and therefore require no entanglement in principle, raising the fundamental question of whether and how entangling gates help or hinder the variational search. We investigate this question for MaxCut by introducing two complementary control mechanisms that provide smooth, monotonic control over hardware-efficient ansatz (HEA) entanglement as quantified by the Meyer-Wallach measure $Q$, and by benchmarking against QAOA as a problem-structured reference. Tracking the entanglement trajectory $Q(t)$ throughout VQA training reveals that when the ansatz grants the optimizer indirect control over entanglement through its parameters, it consistently drives entanglement down. In line with this tendency, a fully separable ansatz outperforms all entangled hardware-efficient configurations, establishing a monotonic relationship: less problem-agnostic entanglement yields better performance. In contrast, QAOA, whose entanglement is structurally derived from the problem Hamiltonian, maintains high entanglement yet achieves competitive solution quality, demonstrating that entanglement structure, not merely quantity, determines its utility. These findings suggest that HEAs for diagonal Hamiltonians are inappropriate and that variational approaches to combinatorial optimization should prioritize problem-structured circuit designs.

title: Security of binary-modulated optical key distribution against quantum-enhanced coherent eavesdropping
abstract: Abstract Optical key distribution protects the physical layer of communication links by taking advantage of the inherent noise present in the photodetection process. It allows for efficient generation of a shared random key between two distant users that is secure against passive eavesdropping and can be subsequently used for cryptographic purposes. Moreover, it can be straightforwardly implemented over standard intensity modulation and direct detection links, making it an attractive alternative to quantum key distribution. Here we present a comprehensive security analysis against more powerful eavesdroppers possessing the ability to perform either coherent detection, or even quantum-optimal measurements on the intercepted transmission.

title: Localizing and Repairing Backdoor-Sensitive Layers in Pre-trained Language Models for Secure Fine-Tuning
abstract: Task-agnostic backdoor attacks can contaminate pre-trained language models (PLMs) in a way that survives downstream adaptation, even under full fine-tuning, making it difficult for practitioners to trust third-party checkpoints. Existing defenses often rely on privileged assumptions (e.g., access to poisoned data or trigger/target knowledge), thereby limiting their applicability in realistic settings. We present DiSec (Disentanglement of potentially adversarial weights for Secure fine-tuning), a robust and label-efficient purification framework that uses only clean auxiliary text and does not rely on downstream supervision or attack signatures. DiSec elicits model-internal signals from this clean data to separate suspicious parameter components that are inconsistent with benign behavior, and then flags anomalous structures by jointly leveraging complementary spectral and generative views of outliers. Finally, DiSec performs a structure-preserving repair via layer-local prototype-based mean correction, yielding an idempotent update that depends only on non-adversarial statistics. Across diverse downstream classification tasks and PLM backdoor strategies, DiSec substantially suppresses attack success while preserving clean-task utility, offering a practical path to securing fully fine-tuned PLMs before deployment.

title: Anomaly management in unmanned aerial vehicles: A systematic literature review
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications such as logistics, surveillance, disaster response, and urban air mobility. While their autonomy enables powerful capabilities, it also introduces vulnerabilities due to hardware faults, software defects, communication failures, and adversarial interference. This survey presents a comprehensive review of research studies closely related to UAV anomalies published between 2015 and 2025, covering 111 papers from academic and industrial sources. We introduce a unified five-pillar taxonomy—anomaly generation, prevention, detection, recovery, and analysis—that organizes existing work across the full anomaly management lifecycle. In contrast to prior surveys that focus primarily on detection algorithms, our review integrates operational and regulatory perspectives, explicitly linking technical anomalies to policy enforcement and compliance requirements. We systematically compare detection techniques, datasets, simulators, and evaluation practices, revealing significant fragmentation in datasets, limited real-world validation, and a lack of standardized real-time benchmarks. Our synthesis highlights key research challenges, including the sim-to-real gap, limited interpretability of learning-based detectors, and the scarcity of policy-aware anomaly management frameworks. Based on these findings, we outline emerging research opportunities for adaptive, explainable, and benchmark-driven anomaly management systems that support safe, transparent, and reliable UAV operations. We release our metadata for all the papers reviewed, as well as filters for easy sorting at [1].

title: IoT Device Fingerprinting and Impersonation Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, security has become a significant challenge— particularly impersonation attacks, where an adversary masquerades as a trusted device. In this paper, we introduce a machine learning framework that fingerprints IoT devices and catches impersonation attacks by analyzing their network traffic. We train a Random Forest classifier on statistical features extracted solely from benign traffic of nine commercial IoT devices (N-BaIoT dataset). The model achieves highly accurate device identification with a weighted accuracy and F1-score of 98.63% and can clearly distinguish different device types. For impersonation detection, we use the fingerprinting model’s confidence: traffic that does not match any known device with high certainty is flagged as an impostor. The confidence-based anomaly detection scheme, evaluated on Mirai and Gafgyt attack traffic, achieves a 93.5% true positive rate at a 1.2% false positive rate. The approach is entirely passive, requiring no modifications to the devices themselves, is sufficiently lightweight for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices, and produces interpretable results. Our findings demonstrate that network behavioural fingerprinting is a viable and practical security primitive for IoT environments.

title: The Einstein Test and Beyond: The Architecture of the Epistemic Zero
abstract: Demis Hassabis’s Einstein Test defines the ultimate benchmark for Artificial General Intelligence: could a system trained exclusively on pre-1911 knowledge autonomously derive General Relativity? The AI industry reads this as a scale challenge—a problem of compute and data—epitomised by Dario Amodei’s declared goal of building “a moat of the countries of geniuses in a data center.” This paper argues that this dominant Silicon Valley interpretation rests on a profound Ptolemaic assumption: that intelligence is a discrete stock that can be hoarded inside a single isolated agent. We advance a unified structural critique across three fronts. First, large-scale transformer systems are mathematically constrained to function as Stochastic Guessing Engines: thermodynamic probability samplers that intrinsically lack a semantic zero—a stable, addressable coordinate for honest epistemic absence. Without such a zero, the architecture is mechanically forced to hallucinate. Second, Tony McCaffrey’s Obscure Features Hypothesis—formalised in the McCaffrey–Spector Non-Enumerability Theorem—demonstrates that genuine novelty depends on biologically situated friction that a closed manifold cannot pre-enumerate. Third, using the Reverse Einstein Test as a continuous narrative thread, we synthesise seven independent impossibility arguments into a strict chronological cascade, culminating in the Gödel–Gauss-Bonnet proof that a sealed manifold with no puncture to reality is necessarily and irremediably incomplete. We ground our resolution in the Semiotic Web, introducing two foundational objects: the Canonical Concept Identity (CCI) and the Contextual Tokum Instance (CTI). Together they resolve the Semantic Field Equation and satisfy Yann LeCun’s four criteria for Autonomous Machine Intelligence. A key architectural consequence is the Semantic Light Cone of Care: each agent (holon) in a distributed network has a precise, mathematically bounded domain of verified knowledge and concern. This bounded self-awareness enables polycomputing across trillions of low-power edge devices—each node knowing exactly what it knows and what it does not—and allows seamless voluntary cooperation via Burgess’s Promise Theory across the platonic address space. The paper concludes by addressing Satya Nadella’s observation that “we are one sort of innovation away from the entire regime changing,” arguing that the required innovation is not a new scaling law but a notation inversion: the introduction of a semantic zero and a cryptographically verified observer’s mark. Once instantiated, the debate between AGI and Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence becomes as irrelevant as the geocentric model after Copernicus. Intelligence is not a stock inside a machine; it is a flow that reduces systemic stress through gap-closure, a property of a distributed, substrate-independent network organised in holonic federation—the Copernican Completion of Artificial Intelligence.

title: Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer Accuracy in Multilingual vs. English Intermediate-Task Training for Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. title: An Adaptive SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on Dynamic Data Schema Adjustment
abstract: Class imbalance remains a critical challenge in the fields of machine learning and data mining, where standard classifiers often exhibit a strong bias toward the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind linear interpolation strategy often introduces noise and causes severe class overlapping, especially near the decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Schema SMOTE (AS-SMOTE) algorithm based on dynamic data schema adjustment. The core idea of AS-SMOTE is to dynamically analyze the local density and spatial characteristics of minority class samples prior to generating new instances. By computing a boundary awareness factor and assessing feature variances within the local neighborhood, the algorithm adaptively constructs a feature schema weight for each dimension. This schema weight is then integrated into a dynamic regulation vector that constrains the interpolation process. When generating new samples, the algorithm automatically balances generalization capability and pattern adherence: it allows standard random interpolation in safe minority regions, while strictly confining the synthetic instances along the tightly distributed feature "schemas" near the decision boundaries. Theoretical framework analysis demonstrates that AS-SMOTE effectively prevents synthetic samples from invading the majority class space, preserves the local topological structure of the minority class, and enhances the classification performance and robustness of downstream models on imbalanced datasets.

When generating new samples, the algorithm automatically balances generalization capability and pattern adherence: it allows standard random interpolation in safe minority regions, while strictly confining the synthetic instances along the tightly distributed feature "schemas" near the decision boundaries. Theoretical framework analysis demonstrates that AS-SMOTE effectively prevents synthetic samples from invading the majority class space, preserves the local topological structure of the minority class, and enhances the classification performance and robustness of downstream models on imbalanced datasets.

title: A Semantic Constraint SMOTE Over-sampling Method for Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining, widely observed in real-world scenarios such as credit fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. The scarcity of minority class samples often forces traditional classification models to severely bias toward the majority class during training, thereby drastically reducing the recognition accuracy of critical minority cases. As one of the most classic over-sampling techniques, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates structural imbalance by performing linear interpolation between neighboring minority samples. However, traditional SMOTE relies solely on geometric distance in the feature space, completely ignoring the inherent business logic and semantic constraints of the underlying data. Consequently, the synthesized virtual samples often violate real-world rule logic consistency, introducing a multitude of invalid "phantom samples" or heavy noise. To address this critical flaw, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm incorporating semantic constraints, termed SC-SMOTE (Semantic Constraint SMOTE). This approach translates domain expert knowledge and logical rules into mathematical semantic constraint functions, embedding a new neighbor filtering mechanism and a boundary projection correction strategy into the traditional interpolation process. This paper comprehensively details the theoretical foundation, mathematical modeling, and algorithmic workflow of SC-SMOTE. The proposed algorithm not only expands the minority class within the geometric space but also rigorously guarantees the validity and rationality of the generated data within the semantic space. This research offers a novel paradigm for empowering data-driven machine learning models with expert-guided knowledge.

title: Attention-route SMOTE: Oversampling via Attention Flow Guided Generation Paths
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, where standard classifiers often exhibit a bias towards the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its reliance on local Euclidean distances and random linear interpolation frequently leads to over-sampling in noisy or overlapping regions, while failing to preserve the global topological structure of the data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel oversampling algorithm named Attention-route SMOTE. Instead of blindly interpolating between geometric neighbors, the proposed method leverages the self-attention mechanism to explicitly model the global feature correlations among minority class samples, thereby constructing an "attention flow matrix." During the synthesis process, new samples are generated along optimized attention paths, further corrected by an attention context vector that integrates global manifold trends. This attention-guided routing ensures that the synthesized samples not only inherit local characteristics but also conform to the underlying global data distribution. Consequently, Attention-route SMOTE effectively expands the minority class space, enhances sample diversity, and maintains distinct class boundaries without introducing structural noise.

title: A Novel Enterprise AI Classification Framework for Business Transformation: A Structured Literature Review and Integration of AI Types and Autonomy Levels
abstract: Enterprise investment in artificial intelligence has reached an unprecedented scale across national, regional, and organisational levels of the economy, yet transformation outcomes remain highly variable. Recent global research indicates that the majority of enterprise AI investments produce no measurable profit-and-loss impact, with only a minority of organisations extracting material enterprise-level value. Without an integrated classification framework that allows enterprises to deploy, govern, and create value from the full range of AI technologies and autonomy levels across enterprise functions, the risks of misallocated investment, fragmented deployment, and unrealised return remain difficult to mitigate. A structured literature review on AI classification reveals that existing frameworks do not integrate AI technology types, operational autonomy levels, and concrete enterprise applications in a single classification structure that can support enterprise AI-driven transformation decisions. To address this gap, this paper proposes the Enterprise AI Classification Framework, a novel classification model that integrates six AI technology types with six autonomy levels in a 6 × 6 matrix of 36 combinations, each corresponding to concrete business applications across enterprise functions. A computational pilot study (n = 20 cases for case-based coding validation and 12 LLM-simulated personas × 30 vignettes for role-specific hypothesis pre-specification) provides preliminary evidence of substantially higher classification coverage than four baseline frameworks and pre-specifies role-divergence hypotheses for a planned empirical validation, with all design choices locked in an OSF pre-registration; reliability point estimates exceed the pre-specified α≥0.70 threshold at the pilot scale, with bootstrapped confidence intervals expected to tighten under the full-corpus run in the follow-up study. An interview-based empirical validation with approximately 250 decision-makers and practitioners across 20 industries is in preparation.

title: A Logic of Limited Belief with Introspection Based on Possible Worlds
abstract: The starting point of this paper is earlier work, where we proposed an epistemic logic which characterizes the beliefs of a knowledge-based agent in terms of increasing levels of complexity. At the lowest level, the agent is only able to draw simple conclusions from its knowledge base. Higher levels lead to more and more inferences and computing the beliefs at any particular level turns out to be tractable. What makes this logic arguably appealing is the fact that the underlying semantics is based on possible worlds. However, the work is still limited in that only beliefs about what is true in the world are considered, that is, an agent's beliefs about its own beliefs are ignored. In this paper we will close this gap and generalize the earlier work by proposing a model of limited belief where an agent is able to fully introspect on its own beliefs without sacrificing tractability.

title: The Historical Framing Problem: Temporal Modeling of Interactions between Tangible and Intangible Cultural Heritage
abstract: The distinction between tangible and intangible cultural heritage (CH) is problematic for modeling interactions between material and immaterial expressions of the arts and culture. This hinders capturing changes in CH objects in their cultural contexts, necessary to understand their social functions and symbolic meanings. This paper addresses this problem twofold. First, after providing a theoretical-historiographical overview of the concepts of framing and historical time, the present paper proposes a historical frames system consisting of reference frames and historical frames. A model of historical frames allowing for spatiotemporal views of storylines is discussed in more detail. Second, a framework of ontological modules is provided that expresses the historical frames by extending existing ontologies. As most interactions between tangible and intangible CH are less defined, particular attention is paid to the modeling of ephemeral events. The model is designed using five types of such interactions in a case study of the late 12th century reliquary shrine of St. Servatius in Maastricht and the festivities around it. The outcomes are four modules describing 1) functions of objects in context, 2) frames capturing different temporal events, in particular ephemeral events, 3) the evolution of material and immaterial objects, and 4) peculiarities of ephemeral events and objects.

title: Trust-Aware Client Scoring in Federated Learning via Contrastive Attention and Representation Clustering
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, but its decentralized architecture presents significant trust challenges, particularly in the presence of adversarial clients. Most existing defenses rely on prior assumptions, trusted data, or heuristic trust models, thereby limiting their robustness. In this paper, we propose a novel zero-trust scoring mechanism for federated learning that infers client reliability during aggregation, without assuming any prior trust information or access to clean reference data. Our approach assigns trust scores based solely on representation-level information, without access to client data. Each client creates a compact representation via an intra-client self-attention pooling step, and on the server side, an inter-client attention module compares all client representations to produce initial trust scores. These trust scores are then regularized using a hybrid clustering component (K-Means combined with DBSCAN for outlier detection), employing a contrastive cluster-aware loss that promotes consistency within coherent client groups while suppressing the influence of adversarial participants. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and GTSRB demonstrate that the proposed method effectively isolates adversarial behavior, generalizes to unseen clients from the same data distribution, and improves global model performance under diverse poisoningbased adversarial scenarios. This zero-trust, self-organizing framework provides a resilient and practical solution for trustaware aggregation in federated learning.

title: Recurrent Actor-Critic Navigation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in Arbitrary-Shape Obstacle-Dense Environments via Temporally-Augmented Observation
abstract: Reactive navigation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in cluttered environments using only local sensor feedback is severely hampered by partial observability: irregularly-shaped obstacles can disappear from the sensor’s instantaneous field of view, causing wrap-around collisions and local-minima traps. However, existing Reinforcement Learning approaches only partially address these challenges, as they commonly assume regularly shaped, often circular or convex, obstacles. This work proposes a lightweight recurrent extension of the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm that tackles navigation in cluttered environments populated with arbitrary-shape obstacles. By augmenting the agent’s observation with a sliding window of recent states, the resulting Temporally-Augmented Observation TD3 (TAO-TD3) feeds stacked observations through a recurrent feature backbone, enabling the policy to better infer obstacle structure from temporal information. Benchmark evaluations across five environments with increasing obstacle density and count demonstrate that TAO-TD3 consistently reduces collisions and improves goal-reaching rates relative to memory-less Reinforcement Learning.

title: Correlative Reciprocal-Space and Spectral Mapping of the Quantum Microstructure in High-Performance Epitaxial Materials for Superconducting Qubits
abstract: Superconducting qubit technology is among the most promising hardware platform for quantum computing due to its fast gate operation, manufacturing scalability, and architectural flexibility [1]. A key figure of merit that dictates quantum computing functionality is the qubit’s coherence time, which needs to be maximized in order to bring quantum computing to the practical and scalable realm [2]. In particular, the T1 relaxation time—now on the order of milliseconds—can be enhanced with materials engineering, as amorphous dielectrics and crystallographic defects, among other factors, are known to induce decoherence [3-7]. Current state-of-the-art superconducting qubit devices use amorphous AlOx sandwiched between two superconducting Al electrodes as the Josephson junction (JJ), a key element in the transmon qubit, but amorphous dielectrics introduce two-level system (TLS) loss that underlie decoherence [8]. For this reason, numerous efforts have explored crystalline dielectrics as a replacement for amorphous AlOx, since single-crystal materials do not suffer from the lack of long-range order and sub-stoichiometry that comprise TLS defects [9-12]. However, none of these alternative materials choices have been able to surpass, let alone replicate, the performance of Al-AlOx-Al JJs. In this work, we fabricate superconducting quantum devices using a novel heteroepitaxial TiN/γ-Al2O3/TiN tri-layer stack grown on sapphire (Fig. 1a) and find that the measured microwave loss of the single-crystal γ-Al2O3 dielectric is lower than that of amorphous AlOx by two orders of magnitude. For qubits made with this tri-layer to transcend the coherence of incumbent Al-AlOx-Al, the structural, chemical, and electronic defects that induce TLS loss in these materials need to be well understood. Towards this end, we combine scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) methods to highlight structural and interfacial complexity across length scales, ultimately identifying loss sources in the TiN/γ-Al2O3/TiN heteroepitaxial tri-layer. With atomic-resolution imaging and four-dimensional (4D-)STEM nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED), we find that the dielectric γ-Al2O3 layer, though single-crystalline (Fig. 1b), suffers from the formation of antiphase boundaries (Fig. 1c), which can host strong local electric fields and enhance lossy dielectric response [13]. Correlated with these nanoscale planar defects is uniformly distributed elastic strain, on the order of 6%, between the lattice-mismatched γ-Al2O3 and TiN (Fig. 1d). In other words, the dielectric layer is fully strained to match the underlying metal layer; such high strain can distort local bonding environments and thus create new TLSs or shift existing TLSs into resonance. Beyond imperfections within the bulk of the dielectric layer, there are noteworthy interfacial defects: roughening of both TiN/γ-Al2O3 interfaces deviate from atomically flat boundaries (Fig. 1c), while anion interdiffusion across both interfaces, as evident from core-loss electron energy-loss spectral (EELS) maps (Fig. 1e), leave behind vacancies and undercoordinated metal atoms, thereby creating 1.5 – 2 nm nonstoichiometric diffuse interfacial layers, both of which can cause TLS loss. In the superconducting TiN layers, we again use NBED to identify 180°-reflected specular twinned domains, indicating distinct heteroepitaxial relationships of [111]TiN//[0006]Al2O3 and [002¯]TiN//[22¯02¯]Al2O3 (Fig. 2a) [14]. Crystal twinning of the TiN epilayer is not only spatially distributed at the nanoscale, as shown using virtual dark-field (VDF) images (Fig. 2b), but is also widespread at the microscale, as shown using SEM electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) (Fig. 2c). While microwave performance is not limited by a single factor, it is clear that defective quantum microstructure across length scales collectively contribute to dielectric loss, and in turn, TLS-related decoherence. By correlating nanoscale crystallographic and spectroscopic information with microscale diffraction measurements, our work can guide interface engineering during material growth, paving the way towards further improvements in quantum device performance. Cross-sectional samples were prepared by subsequent 30 kV, 8 kV and 5 kV Xe+ plasma focused ion beam (FIB) using the Thermo Scientific Helios 5 Hydra CX DualBeam Plasma FIB/SEM. Samples were then plasma cleaned using South Bay Technology PC-2000 Plasma Cleaner with a 3:1 mixture of Ar:O2 gas at 20∼40 W RF power for 15 s at 150 mTorr. High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF-) and annular bright-field (ABF-) STEM images were collected on a probe-corrected JEOL JEM-ARM200CF S/TEM operating at 200 kV using JEOL detectors. The STEM convergence angle, HAADF collection angle, and ABF collection angle were 27 mrad, 90 – 370 mrad, and 23 mrad, respectively. EELS data were collected on a JEOL JEM-ARM300F GrandARM S/TEM operating at 300 kV using the Gatan GIF Continuum K3 IS system. The data were collected using a 2.5 mm aperture and a 750 eV wide energy slit at a dispersion of 0.18 eV/Ch and a camera length of 2 cm. 4D-STEM data were collected on the same microscope and detector system using a 0.5 – 1.5 mrad convergence angle and a 20 eV wide energy slit at a camera length of 4 cm. All STEM data processing was performed using the Gatan Microscopy Suite software. Top-down EBSD measurements were performed in the Thermo Scientific Helios 5 CX DualBeam FIB/SEM at 25 kV using the Oxford Symmetry S3 detector. evidence.title: Correlative Reciprocal-Space and Spectral Mapping of the Quantum Microstructure in High-Performance Epitaxial Materials for Superconducting Qubits
evidence.abstract: Superconducting qubit technology is among the most promising hardware platform for quantum computing due to its fast gate operation, manufacturing scalability, and architectural flexibility [1]. A key figure of merit that dictates quantum computing functionality is the qubit’s coherence time, which needs to be maximized in order to bring quantum computing to the practical and scalable realm [2]. In particular, the T1 relaxation time—now on the order of milliseconds—can be enhanced with materials engineering, as amorphous dielectrics and crystallographic defects, among other factors, are known to induce decoherence [3-7]. Current state-of-the-art superconducting qubit devices use amorphous AlOx sandwiched between two superconducting Al electrodes as the Josephson junction (JJ), a key element in the transmon qubit, but amorphous dielectrics introduce two-level system (TLS) loss that underlie decoherence [8]. For this reason, numerous efforts have explored crystalline dielectrics as a replacement for amorphous AlOx, since single-crystal materials do not suffer from the lack of long-range order and sub-stoichiometry that comprise TLS defects [9-12]. However, none of these alternative materials choices have been able to surpass, let alone replicate, the performance of Al-AlOx-Al JJs. In this work, we fabricate superconducting quantum devices using a novel heteroepitaxial TiN/γ-Al2O3/TiN tri-layer stack grown on sapphire (Fig. 1a) and find that the measured microwave loss of the single-crystal γ-Al2O3 dielectric is lower than that of amorphous AlOx by two orders of magnitude. For qubits made with this tri-layer to transcend the coherence of incumbent Al-AlOx-Al, the structural, chemical, and electronic defects that induce TLS loss in these materials need to be well understood. Towards this end, we combine scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) methods to highlight structural and interfacial complexity across length scales, ultimately identifying loss sources in the TiN/γ-Al2O3/TiN heteroepitaxial tri-layer. With atomic-resolution imaging and four-dimensional (4D-)STEM nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED), we find that the dielectric γ-Al2O3 layer, though single-crystalline (Fig. 1b), suffers from the formation of antiphase boundaries (Fig. 1c), which can host strong local electric fields and enhance lossy dielectric response [13]. Correlated with these nanoscale planar defects is uniformly distributed elastic strain, on the order of 6%, between the lattice-mismatched γ-Al2O3 and TiN (Fig. 1d). In other words, the dielectric layer is fully strained to match the underlying metal layer; such high strain can distort local bonding environments and thus create new TLSs or shift existing TLSs into resonance. Beyond imperfections within the bulk of the dielectric layer, there are noteworthy interfacial defects: roughening of both TiN/γ-Al2O3 interfaces deviate from atomically flat boundaries (Fig. 1c), while anion interdiffusion across both interfaces, as evident from core-loss electron energy-loss spectral (EELS) maps (Fig. 1e), leave behind vacancies and undercoordinated metal atoms, thereby creating 1.5 – 2 nm nonstoichiometric diffuse interfacial layers, both of which can cause TLS loss. In the superconducting TiN layers, we again use NBED to identify 180°-reflected specular twinned domains, indicating distinct heteroepitaxial relationships of [111]TiN//[0006]Al2O3 and [002¯]TiN//[22¯02¯]Al2O3 (Fig. 2a) [14]. Crystal twinning of the TiN epilayer is not only spatially distributed at the nanoscale, as shown using virtual dark-field (VDF) images (Fig. 2b), but is also widespread at the microscale, as shown using SEM electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) (Fig. 2c). While microwave performance is not limited by a single factor, it is clear that defective quantum microstructure across length scales collectively contribute to dielectric loss, and in turn, TLS-related decoherence. By correlating nanoscale crystallographic and spectroscopic information with microscale diffraction measurements, our work can guide interface engineering during material growth, paving the way towards further improvements in quantum device performance. title: Heterogeneous fusion of RFS and LRFS filters via optimal transport
abstract: In the heterogeneous random finite set (RFS)-based multi-target tracking where local sensors operate different types of RFS filters, the effective fusion of the heterogeneous posterior information from different RFS filters plays the key role. Our earlier series of companion papers proposed a solution that address the fusion in the first-order moment space, namely probability hypothesis density arithmetic average (PHD-AA). However, existing PHD-AA implementations via Gaussian mixture often face the risk of poor convergence when fitting the weights of local Gaussian components (L-GCs). To overcome this drawback, this paper proposes a fusion framework based on the optimal transport (OT) theory which fits the GC parameters in two steps. That is, the means and covariances of the L-GCs are updated for global consensus through a clustering process. The weights for the updated L-GCs are further determined by solving a semi-coupled OT problem. This two-step optimization strategy does not only preserve the geometric property of the distributions but also ensures a synergistic and robust fitting of all parameters. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed OT-fit method exhibits faster convergence, higher accuracy, and greater stability compared to the traditional integrated squared difference-fit method in both homogeneous and heterogeneous filter fusion scenarios.

title: Named entity recognition in water conservancy field based on multi-feature fusion and boundary perception
abstract: Named entity recognition in the water conservancy field is a crucial step in extracting water conservancy information, playing a key role in constructing water conservancy knowledge graphs and enhancing water conservancy knowledge question answering systems. However, existing methods still face challenges when dealing with text data in the field, including semantic diversity of entities, ambiguity in entity boundaries and insufficient feature utilization, resulting in limited recognition performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Named Entity Recognition Model based on Multi-feature Fusion and Boundary Perception (MFBP-NER). The model extracts multi-source features from three dimensions namely characters, pinyin, and dictionaries to obtain a more semantically rich feature representation. On this basis, an Adaptive Gating Fusion (AGF) mechanism is proposed to achieve dynamic weighting and effective fusion among multiple features, fully exploiting the deep semantic interaction relationships across different feature dimensions. Meanwhile, a BiGRU network is employed to further capture context dependencies and long-distance relationships within sequences. Additionally, a boundary perception module is incorporated into the global pointer framework to model semantic dependency relationships between spans, thereby enhancing entity boundary differences and enabling more accurately determine entity boundary. To evaluate the performance of MFBP-NER, experiments are conducted on three datasets with varying granularity. The results show that the proposed model achieves higher F1 scores compared to baseline models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in named entity recognition within the water conservancy field. It provides a viable technical foundation for constructing water conservancy knowledge graphs and developing question answering systems.

title: A blended sentiment analysis, large language model, and multi-criteria decision-making (BSLMM) approach to sustainable product innovation
abstract: Abstract Owing to the growing popularity of electronic marketplaces, individual online retailers must evaluate a large volume of customer text reviews to gather feedback about consumer preferences and support sustainable product evaluation. Product evaluation involves multiple product attributes simultaneously, making it a multi-criteria decision-making problem. While traditional sentiment analysis captures isolated customer insights, this approach is subject to three key limitations. These are reliance on context-blind extraction methods for attribute identification, subjective weighting schemes that cannot handle correlated criteria, and insufficient treatment of linguistic uncertainty arising from inter-reviewer variability in sentiment intensity. To address this, this study introduces BSLMM (BERT-based Sentiment analysis with Language Models and Multi-Criteria Decision Making), a systematic framework that integrates BERT for contextual attribute extraction and aspect-level sentiment scoring, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for transforming correlated attributes into independent criteria with objectively derived weights, and fuzzy COPRAS for ranking product alternatives. This study contributes a data analytics framework that blends sentiment analysis, pre-trained language models and MCDM for product benchmarking and development. Furthermore, it offers practitioners a low-cost data-driven approach to competitive product development towards sustainable innovation.

title: Computing the Molecular Ground State Energy in a Restricted Active Space Using Quantum Annealing
abstract: ABSTRACT Calculating the molecular ground‐state energy is a central challenge in computational chemistry. Conventional methods such as the Complete Active Space Configuration Interaction scale exponentially with molecular size, limiting their applicability to large molecules. Quantum computing offers a promising alternative by mapping molecular Hamiltonians to qubits, enabling cheaper computational scaling. Previous studies have shown that it is possible to formulate molecular ground state calculations as discrete optimization problems, addressable by quantum annealing. However, these efforts have been limited by previous generations of hardware and suboptimal annealing techniques. Here, the ground‐state problem is mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian using the Xian–Bias–Kas (XBK) method. By taking advantage of enhanced qubit connectivity and shorter embedding chains, it is solved with a more than doubled probability of achieving Hartree–Fock–level solutions with respect to the most advanced predecessor. Advanced annealing strategies extend Hartree–Fock–level accuracy to significantly larger problem instances, enabling solutions that use nearly 2.5 times more physically embedded qubits than the largest cases previously reported and allowing to improve annealing results by two orders of magnitude, reaching an energy difference of 0.120 Hartree relative to Hartree‐Fock. These results show tangible progress toward practical quantum annealing applications in the NISQ era.
